Official Gazette of The GCC - Bureau of Technical Secretariat for Anti Injurious Practices in International Trade Volume (9)
Introduction
In compliance with the basic objectives of the Cooperation Council for the Arab
States of the Gulf, and in conformity with the objectives of the GCC Unified Economic
Convention seeking to achieve economic integration among GCC member states, and
aware of the crucial role played by GCC industries in the economies of the GCC member
states, it becomes vital for the member states to take necessary measures against dumping,
subsidy and increase of imports, which cause injury, threat of injury, or retardation to
GCC industries.
Pursuant to Article 86 of the Rules of Implementation of the GCC Common Law on
Antidumping, Countervailing Measures and Safeguards (Amended) which states, “The
Technical Secretariat issues an Official Gazette where it publishes all publications required
under this Common Law and its Rules of Implementation”. Hereby, GCC-Bureau of
Technical Secretariat for Anti Injurious Practices in International Trade pleased to publish
the Notice Volume No (9) of the Official Gazette of GCC- Bureau of Technical Secretariat
for Anti-Injurious Practices in International Trade
.

The Secretariat General of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf (GCC)
GCC- Bureau of Technical Secretariat for Anti Injurious Practices in International Trade
Imposition of a provisional safeguard measure
against GCC imports of Ferro-silico-manganese
In conformity with the GCC Common Law on Anti-Dumping, Countervailing and
Safeguard Measures and its Rules of Implementation (Amended) (the Regulation), and
upon the decision of the Permanent Committee for Anti Injurious Practices in International
Trade (Permanent Committee) No. (2/2S/2016) to initiate a safeguard investigation
(1)
against the Increase in GCC Imports of Ferro-Silico-Manganese and the Permanent
Committee›s decision No. (3/2S/2016)) to impose a provisional safeguard measures
against the GCC imports of the product under investigation pursuant to the provisions of
Article (73) of the Regulation and Article (6) of the Agreement on Safeguards, the GCC
bureau of technical secretariat for anti-injurious practices in international trade (GCC-
TSAIP) announces that a provisional safeguard measures will be applied against GCC
imports of the product under investigation according to the following:
1. Product subject to the provisional safeguard measure
Ferro-Silico-Manganese is the product under investigation which is classified under
the GCC-Unified Tariff Code (72023000)
2. Duration of provisional safeguard measures
The provisional measures will be applied for (200) days
3. Form of the provisional safeguard measures
Provisional safeguard measures will take the form of tariff increase by (21%) of CIF
value against GCC›s imports of Ferro-silico-manganese.
4. Basis of the preliminary determination
4. 1 Increase in imports in absolute and relative terms
The imports volume of Ferro-silico-manganese increased significantly in both
absolute terms and relative to the production of the complainant industry during
(1) Notice concerning the initiation of a safeguard investigation against the GCC imports of Ferro-
silico-manganese, in the Official Gazette - Bureau of technical secretariat for anti-injurious practices in
international trade volume (8).

the period 2012 – 2015. The imports according to the table below increased by
267.01% during 2015 compared to 2012. Relatively to the production, the imports
increased during 2015 by 351.48% compared to 2012.

Imports Volume (ton) 34,273.74 40,799.08 112,673.15 125,786.84

Accordingly, it is revealed to GCC-TSAIP the existence of a recent, sudden, sharp
and significant increase in imports of Ferro-silico-manganese in both absolute terms
and relative to the production.
4. 2 Determination of serious injury
The following table shows the evolution of the imports› volume and its impact on
the most important economic and financial indicators of the complainant industry
during the period 2012 -2015.

It is determined that the relative and absolute increase in imports caused a serious
injury to the complainant industry and that the delay in taking action would cause
damage that would be difficult to repair. The above table shows the most important
aspects of the serious injury as follows:
- Decline in volume of production and capacity utilization during 2015 by 18.17%
compared to 2012.
- Decline in domestic sales during 2015 by 8.47% compared to 2012 despite of the
GCC market growth, and a decline in its market share by 49.49% during the same
period.
- Increase in inventory volume during 2015 by 44, 63% compared to 2012.
- Deterioration of the cash flow by (-511.16) % during 2015 compared to 2012.
- Deterioration of the profitability of the industry and its ROI during the period
2012-2015 respectively by (-325.92) % and (-347) %.
- Decline in employment by 39.07% during 2015 compared to 2012.
4. 3 Causal link
GCC-TSAIP examined the causal link between the increase in imports and the
serious injury caused to the complainant industry by studying known factors other
than imports which might contribute to the serious injury, such as export performance,
contraction in demand or changes in the patterns of consumption, developments in
technology and trade restrictive practices, and has concluded the following:
- The serious injury suffered by the GCC industry coincided with the recent, sharp,
sudden and significant increase in imports of Ferro-silico-manganese in both
absolute terms and relative to the production.
- Other factors such as contraction in demand and changes in the patterns of
consumption, trade restrictive practices, developments in technology or export
performance didn’t contribute in the serious injury on the complainant industry,
and this injury is due to the increase in imports under complaint.
Accordingly, it became clear to GCC-TSAIP that there are sufficient evidence of
the existence of a causal link between the increase in imports and the serious injury
on the domestic industry.

Official Gazette of The GCC - Bureau of Technical Secretariat for Anti Injurious Practices in International Trade Volume (9)
4. 4 Critical circumstances
When examining the injury indicators, GCC-TSAIP found that there is an
overall deterioration of economic indicators and worsening of financial crises of the
complainant industry during the period 2012- 2015. The data showed a significant
decline in production and sales volume as well as a significant increase in inventory
volume, prompting the GCC industry to sell at low prices not covering its cost of
production, which contributed to the accumulation of the debt in the short term and
the inability of the company to meet its financial obligations. This is in addition to the
board of Directors decision dated 02/05/2015 about the suspension of production and
the closure of the plant in case no solution is found.
Accordingly, it is revealed to GCC-TSAIP through the data and the evidence
submitted in the complaint that there are critical circumstances which may lead the
complainant industry to bankruptcy and plant closure and layoffs, and that any delay
of adopting a provisional safeguard measure would cause damage which it would be
difficult to repair. This situation requires the application of the provisions of Article
(6) of the Agreement on Safeguards and Article (73) of the Regulation, in order to
remedy the serious injury faced by the complainant industry.
5. Developing countries exempted from the provisional safeguard measure
In accordance with the requirements of Special and Differential Treatment
provisions’ for developing countries members of WTO and pursuant to the provisions
of article (76) of the Regulation, provisional safeguard measures will not apply
against the imports of Ferro-silico-manganese originating in the following developing
countries members of WTO:
Afghanistan; Albania; Angola; Antigua and Barbuda; Argentina; Armenia;
Bangladesh; Barbados; Belize; Benin; Bolivia, Plurinational State of; Botswana;
Brazil; Brunei Darussalam; Burkina Faso; Burundi; Cabo Verde; Cambodia;
Cameroon; Central African Republic; Chad; Chile; China; Chinese Taipei; Colombia;
